title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Internal Revenue Service relating to "Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales".
short_title: Repeal of the Internal Revenue Service rule on Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating…
committees: H-Ways and Means Committee: Referred To 2025-01-21 -> Markup By 2025-02-26 -> Reported By 2025-02-28
committee_votes: Ways and Means Committee 2025-02-26: Ordered reported - 26-16
summary: This joint resolution nullifies requirements for persons effectuating decentralized financial (DeFi) transactions to report certain information regarding digital asset sales to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies the requirements included in the rule titled Gross Proceeds Reporting by Brokers That Regularly Provide Services Effectuating Digital Asset Sales and issued by the IRS on December 30, 2024. Decentralized finance refers to the suite of financial activities and services that are facilitated by cryptocurrency and intended to be conducted without any sort of reliance on traditional financial tools or intermediaries.

income.magnitude_note: JCT put the revenue loss at about $4 billion over ten years (cost estimate on file: CBO publication 61241). Almost all of the lost revenue is tax that would have been collected from crypto gains that now go unreported.
income.justification: The repeal removes IRS reporting of sales on decentralized crypto platforms, so its benefit is lower effective tax on crypto gains. Crypto ownership and especially decentralized-platform use skew toward higher-income and higher-wealth households, and capital-gain relief moves the score positive under the text rules. The effect is small in dollars and reaches a narrow group, which keeps it out of the higher bands.

households_business.magnitude_note: Decentralized-finance platforms avoid building broker reporting systems; users avoid new tax forms; the Treasury loses roughly $4 billion over ten years.
households_business.justification: The main beneficiaries are the platforms, which no longer have to identify users and report their sales, and the traders whose gains stay unreported. Households that use these platforms get less paperwork, a small plus; everyone else bears the revenue loss.

plain.plain: The reporting rule, which would have covered sales from 2027 on, never takes effect.

plain.one_sentence: Cancels an IRS rule that would have made decentralized crypto exchanges report their users' sales to the IRS starting in 2027.

if_you_are.worker: No direct effect unless you trade crypto on decentralized platforms; those platforms will not send you or the IRS a tax form.
if_you_are.small_business_owner: If you run a decentralized crypto service, you no longer have to collect customer identities and report their sales.

plain.what_it_does_not_do: It does not make crypto gains tax-free; you still owe tax on them, the platform just will not report them.
